{{Quote|I sought to dance among star temples and understand dark time. In truth, I remember little.|The Imprisoned One|<ref name="Thing Found Rep" />}}
'''The Imprisoned One''', known to the [[Sons of Palawa]] as '''the Ghost of the Desert''',<ref name="ghosts">{{TORcite|type=faction|[[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Imperial]]|The Ghosts of the Desert|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref> was a [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] who lived during the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire's]] dominance over [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. His quest for personal power resulted in his own kind imprisoning his consciousness in a [[mind prison]]. His consciousness vessel was eventually rediscovered by the [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]] in the years before the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]].

==Biography==
The Imprisoned One lived sometime during the height of the Infinite Empire. Despite the numerous, galaxy-spanning accomplishments of his race, he sought to enhance his own prestige beyond that of any Rakatan. Seeking to use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and some kind of [[Nanotechnology/Legends|nanotechnology]] to assure his own immortality, he quickly became regarded as a criminal and a heretic amongst his own kind. They hunted him down and extracted his consciousness from his physical body to be placed in a [[Mind prison|mechanical vessel]]. The vessel was placed deep in a cave, to become his eternal prison.<ref name="Thing Found Rep" />

[[File:Imprisoned_One_mind_prison.png|thumb|left|150px|The mind prison in which the Imprisoned One was contained]]
With the eventual fall of the Infinite Empire, he lay dormant and forgotten in his prison for twenty thousands of years. Eventually his mind prison was re-discovered in the years before the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]],<ref name="Last One Out">{{TORcite|type=faction|Republic|Last One Out|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref> by a team of [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]] archaeologists, who built a [[Czerka Secret Weapons Division 7|facility]] around the cave. The Imprisoned One managed to turn the scientists into unthinking drones from inside his prison, by means of the very nanotechnology he had used to attempt his own immortality millennia earlier. Emergency protocols executed by the Czerka staff were effective in isolating the facility and preventing the spread of the Imprisoned One's infection further.<ref name="Thing Found Rep" />

However his influence was still felt in the desert, and a mysterious force transforming those who venture too close to the old [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]] [[Czerka Secret Weapons Division 7|compound]] was known to local nomads, named by the [[Sons of Palawa]] as the "ghost of the desert".<ref name="ghosts" /> [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]] had maps, warning to avoid the "forbidden land", where Czerka constructed their base.<ref name="Journey into Dust">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|Journey into Dust|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref>

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|option=1}}

Decades later, [[Gayem Leksende]], [[Republic Strategic Information Service|Republic Strategic Information Service (SIS)]] and [[Imperial Reclamation Service]] all clashed on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] searching for the Czerka [[Czerka Secret Weapons Division 7|facility]] and artifacts hidden inside. In [[3643 BBY]], an associate of a SIS agent [[Fauler]] was able to find the compound still overrun by augmented walking dead, who constructed Rakata replication machines to manufacture droids and augment more corpses. Gayem Leksende, a Czerka official following his own agenda, was hot on Fauler's associate's trail, and both of them witnessed a holoprojection of the Imprisoned One, stating his plans for a new grand conquest. Fauler's associate disabled the replication machines and attempted to destroy the mind prison, which angered Gayem, who planned to secure it for himself. A confrontation followed and Gayem was killed, after which Fauler's associate left the compound believing to have destroyed the mind prison.<ref name="Thing Found Rep" />

However, as is often the case with [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] technology, the Imprisoned One's mind prison as well as his machines for producing mindless servants self-repaired, and were soon rediscovered again by an [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Imperial]] individual working with the [[Imperial Reclamation Service]]. The individual fought a new batch of droids and augmented dead, proving themselves worthy of Rakatan admiration. Seeing an opportunity in collaboration, the Imprisoned One agreed to serve the Empire, and an imperial took his mind prison to the [[Reclamation Service Outpost 701|Reclamation Service forward outpost]], from where it was supposed to be transported to [[Dromund Kaas]] for future study.<ref name="Thing Found Imp" /> [[Imperial Science Bureau (Sith Empire)|Imperial Science Bureau]] later built a secure "clean room" to study the mind prison; it was rumored that at least one of the researchers lost his mind in the process.<ref name="mail1">{{TORcite|type=message|Tatooine Expedition / Czerka Box|Captain [[Barden Golah|Golah]]}}</ref>

{{EndGame}}

==Behind the scenes==
The Imprisoned One first appeared in [[BioWare]]'s [[2011]] [[Star Wars video games#Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|MMORPG]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. Finding and dealing with the Imprisoned One is the climax of the Tatooine story arc for both the Republic and the Empire. Republic players are given the option of destroying the mind prison to prevent the Imprisoned One from ever being freed (light side), or giving it to a rogue Czerka agent for profit (dark side).<ref name="Thing Found Rep" /> Empire players can also destroy the mind prison (light side) or turn it over to the [[Imperial Reclamation Service]] for exploitation (dark side).<ref name="Thing Found Imp" />
